dataIdInfo.idAbs: Annual five-year age group population estimates by sex for 2015 to 2030 for the national and first-order administrative division levels of Angola were prepared by the U.S. Census Bureau for joining (linking) to shapefiles as attribute data. The estimates are consistent with the midyear national projections from the U.S. Census Bureau International Database (IDB).
dataIdInfo.idPurp: The U.S. Census Bureau is providing annual subnational five-year age group population estimates by sex for Angola for 2015-2030 in a geographic information system (GIS) for users of the Spatial Data Repository, funded by the U.S. President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).
dataIdInfo.idCredit:
CENSUS DATA 2014 Age-Sex Data: Resultados Definitivos do Recenseamento Geral da População e Habitação de Angola 2014, Quadro 1.02: População Residente por Área de Residência, Municípios e Comunas, Segundo os Grandes Grupos Etários e Sexo; Quadro 1.04: População Residente por Grupos Etários e Municípios, Segundo a Área de Residência, Sexo e Índice de Masculinidade; Quadro 1.05: População Residente por Sexo, Municípios e Comunas, Segundo os Grupos Etários. Instituto Nacional de Estatística de Angola. Originally downloaded from http://www.ine.gov.ao/ (data were published in individual provincial reports that are no longer available online, accessed September 05, 2019).
The U.S. Census Bureau cannot guarantee the accuracy of non-U.S. census and survey data.
GEOSPATIAL BOUNDARIES International boundaries coincide with the Large Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset from the U.S. Department of State, Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. Available online at http://geonode.state.gov (accessed April 02, 2024).
Geospatial data for the first-order administrative divisions of Angola were downloaded from GeoBoundaries, available online at http://data.humdata.org/dataset/geoboundaries-admin-boundaries-for-angola, "Angola - Subnational Administrative Boundaries" (accessed April 02, 2024).
The U.S. Census Bureau cannot guarantee the accuracy of boundary placements.
NATIONAL ESTIMATES AND PROJECTIONS U.S. Census Bureau, Population Division. International Database, August 2024 release, available online at http://www.census.gov/idb (accessed April 02, 2024).
NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL AREA NAMES AND CODES (1) U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. NGA Geographic Names Server (GNS), available at http://geonames.nga.mil/geonames/GNSHome/welcome.html (accessed April 02, 2024). Contains geographic area names from the U.S. Board on Geographic Names and the U.S. Government Federal Information Processing System (FIPS) codes. (2) U.S. Government Geopolitical Entities, Names, and Codes (GENC) Standard. NSG Standards Registry, available at http://nsgreg.nga.mil/registries/browse/results.jsp?registryType=genc (accessed April 02, 2024).

Consts.useLimit: U.S. Census Bureau population estimates: None. Acknowledgment of the Census Bureau would be appreciated in products derived from its population estimates. The subnational boundaries used for this shapefile were downloaded by the U.S. Census Bureau from a publicly available source for this product. GeoBoundaries indicates that the Open Database License (ODC-ODbL) applies to the use of these boundaries. The international boundaries are derived from the Large Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset (public domain).

dataIdInfo.suppInfo:
SUBNATIONAL DIVISIONS Angola's first-order administrative divisions: 18 provinces as of the 2014 census.
SHAPEFILES The original shapefile downloaded from GeoBoundaries had 558 polygons and matched the 2014 census communes (third-order administrative divisions) with no changes to the subnational boundaries made by USCB staff. The U.S. Census Bureau aligned the shapefile's national boundary to the Large Scale International Boundary Line (LSIB) dataset from the U.S. Department of State, Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. Finally, the LSIB-aligned shapefile was dissolved into 18 polygons, one for each of Angola's first-order administrative divisions (provinces) as reported by the Instituto Nacional de Estatística de Angola in the 2014 census.
NOTES (1) Original commune level (ADM3) broad age group data (ages 5-14, 15-24, 25-64, and 65 and older) by sex from Quadro 1.02 were disaggregated into 5-year age groups by USCB staff. The data were disaggregated to fit with commune level 5-year age group data for both sexes from Quadro 1.05, as well as municipality level (ADM2) 5-year age group data by sex from Quadro 1.04. (2) The census report for Zaire province was missing commune level data from Quadro 1.05 for age groups 35-39 through 95 and older. The missing data were extrapolated by USCB staff by disaggregating available municipality level 5-year age data from Quadro 1.04.
FEATURE AND ATTRIBUTE DETAILS The 2015-2030 population estimates for Angola's administrative divisions are provided in the following two tables: (1) The Unicode tab-delimited text file (table) "Angola_5yr_age_sex_2015-2030_uscb_jun2024.txt," which can be joined to the shapefile via the common field "GEO_MATCH." (2) The Excel table "Angola_5yr_age_sex_2015-2030_508_uscb_jun2024.xlsx," formatted for accessibility in compliance with Section 508 of the U.S. Government's Federal Rehabilitation Act.
Details on processing of the census data and calculation of 2015-2030 estimates are provided in the "Census Metadata" tab of the Excel file and "Methods for Calculating 5-Year Age Group Population Estimates by Sex for Subnational Areas" document. For the subnational areas, the U.S. Board on Geographic Names (BGN) "approved" names from the NGA Geographic Names Server (cited in the "Credits") were used. For any area that a BGN name was not available, the name from the national census was used. Official codes for the subnational areas from the country's national statistical office, when available, are entered in the "NSO_CODE" field in both the shapefile attribute table and Excel table. Information on any alternative area names or recent name or boundary changes is entered in the "USCBCMNT" field. A partial list of the fields in the Excel and Unicode text files, including all fields identifying geographic names and codes, is provided in the Excel file's "Data Dictionary" tab. The Unicode text file includes the "GEO_MATCH" field and the population estimates. The shapefile includes the geospatial data along with geographic names and codes. More detail on the U.S. Census Bureau subnational age and sex group estimates and maps for PEPFAR can be found in the document "Subnational Population Estimates Components for the Spatial Data Repository." It includes a data dictionary that is similar to that in the Excel table.
METHODOLOGY For more information, see the following methodology documents in the Spatial Data Repository: (1) "U.S. Census Bureau Methodology for SDR Subnational Population Estimates." (2) "U.S. Census Bureau Methods for Calculating 5-Year Age Group Population Estimates by Sex for Subnational Areas." (3) "Instructions for Joining Subnational Population Data to Shapefiles."
ACCESS The U.S. Census Bureau’s products for PEPFAR can be accessed from the Spatial Data Repository at http://spatialdata.dhsprogram.com/home/, which also provides access to data and maps from the DHS (Demographic and Health Surveys) Program. A zipped file containing shapefiles with metadata, an Excel workbook with subnational population estimates, and a Unicode tab-delimited text file is available for each country. PEPFAR products are also available on the Census Bureau website at http://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/demo/international-programs/subnationalpopulation.html for download.
